english.title: Offender under 18 incite sexual activity with a family member - victim boy 13 to 17 - no penetration - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person under the age of 18, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFENDER'S AGE..), whose relation to a boy aged

(A)_[13]_
(B)_[14]_
(C)_[15]_
(D)_[16]_
(E)_[17]_

was within section 27 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RELATIONSHIP..), and you knew or could reasonably be expected to have known was of a description falling within that section, and not reasonably believing he was aged 18 or over, intentionally incited him to

(F)_[touch you]_
(G)_[allow himself to be touched by you]_

and the touching was sexual
english.legislation: Contrary to section 26(1)(a)-(d), (e)(i) and (5) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(ii) A person if sentenced in respect of this offence to at least twelve months imprisonment is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 26).

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Five years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
